The Prophet told a woman weeping beside a grave to fear Allah and be patient.
The Prophet told a woman weeping at a grave that patience is at the first stroke of a calamity, urged his daughter to be patient, and called his tears mercy.
Abu Talha's wife hid their son's death from him until morning, and the Prophet prayed that their night be blessed; real patience is at the first stroke of a calamity.
Abdullah bin Abi Aufa wrote that the Prophet said to be patient when facing the enemy.
A black woman with epilepsy chose patience and Paradise over a cure, asking only not to be uncovered, and Allah promises Paradise to the patient who loses his sight.
Told that an Ansari said a distribution was not meant to please Allah, the Prophet's face changed with anger, and he said Moses was hurt worse yet stayed patient.
None is more patient than Allah with those ascribing children to Him, yet He provides for them; angered by an Ansari's remark, the Prophet recalled Moses, harmed worse yet patient.
Allah says His only reward for a believer who stays patient when a dear one dies is Paradise.
Having given all he had to the Ansar, the Prophet said Allah makes content whoever refrains from begging and gives patience to the patient, the best gift of all.
A woman weeping at a grave rebuffed the Prophet, not recognising him, and when she came to apologise he said patience is at the first stroke of a calamity.
